newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Dlr drops, Sfr up in tiny Hungary FX futures trade.
newsitem.headline: Dlr drops, Sfr up in tiny Hungary FX futures trade.

text.p: Firming Swiss franc and easing dollar were in focus on Hungary's forex futures market on Friday, where few deals were struck on the last day before the Easter holidays.
"Turnover was very low, with foreign bourses closed," said Istvan Koszo, an official of the BUdapest Commodity Exchange (BCE).
The BCE's turnover was a tiny 366 million forint on Friday, down from 3.93 billion forint on Thursday, when trading activity was already low.
The Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) was tradeless.
On the BCE, the Swiss franc stole show with turnover of 1,000 contracts.
Traders in Swiss franc concentrated on the March maturity, which closed steady at 141.00 forints, while September and December firmed marginally, with both maturities untraded.
September dollar firmed 60 fillers to 188.00 forints in 825 contracts, which accounted for all dollar trading.
June dollar rose one forint on an offer, to finish at 182.00 forints, untraded.
The yen (100 units) gained forty fillers for September and December, to close at 155.80 and 162.49 forints respectively, while the March 1998 maturity ended at 168.05 forints, up by 35 pips.
